documents.t: The Maintenance Plan tab displays information related to the open Maintenance Events which exist for the selected asset.

The "Maintenance Plan" tab is used to understand the open "Maintenance Events" which exists for a configuration managed asset. Maintenance Events are persisted in the table "PLUSALFEVENT" The system maintains a single maintenance event for each open corrective (non PM generated) work order that exists for an Asset. Once the work order associated with a Maintenance Event is completed then the event is placed into history. These historical maintenance events are then visible on the Maintenance History tab. In addition, one or more maintenance events are created and managed for each active PM that exists for the selected asset. In the case of active PMs, one maintenance event is managed for each frequency criteria defined on the PM. In addition multiple additional maintenance events may exist for a single PM if there are multiple open work orders for the PM. For example an active PM, with both a calendar and meter based frequency, would display two rows for the PM on the Maintenace Plan tab. Each maintenance event gives information relating to the frequency information and when it is next due, including time or meter units remaining. It may also contain a link to the Work Order (if an open work order exists for the PM) Due to the way the Maintenance Event records are managed by the system, it enables a user to easily view and understand the open scheduled and corrective work that exists for configuration-managed assets. In addition, a full history of all work performed can be easily viewed and understood. The Maintenance Plan also enables the user to view the active maintenance for the selected asset at any "As of Date", either at the current date and time or at a point in time in the past. Note that if a PMs status is changed to INACTIVE then the system will either: Delete the maintenance events(s) if there are no open work orders for the PM. Retain the maintenance event(s) for each open PM work order for the inactive PM. These maintenance event(s) are retained until such time that the work order is completed (at which point they are place into history). If the work order is cancelled then the maintenance event is deleted. Relationship between Maintenance Events and the BDI Maintenance Event records are utilised by the BDI to determine whether specific problem codes should be reported. These are described below: Problem Code Description Explanation EBA Event beyond alert The active PM is past either its Alert Date or Alert Count. EBW Event beyond warning The active PM is past either its Warning Date or Warning Count. EBD Event beyond due The active PM is past either its Due Date or Date Count ENR Event needs review The active PM requires manual review to ensure its Due Date / Count are accurate. Explanation of field values in table columns: Frequency: The frequency value defining the interval at which a PM should be completed. This can be either calendar or meter based. Meter Unit: The meter unit description or calendar unit for the frequency interval. Active: Either the date and time at which the maintenance event became active or the meter count for the asset when maintenance event was activated. In the case of a PM record for a calendar based frequency, this is typically the date and time the PM was last last performed. For a PM record with a meter based frequency this is the meter count when the the PM was last performed. For a corrective maintenance work order this displays the Reported Date of the work order. Since: This field displays either the number of days or meter units recorded since the maintenance event became active. For a calendar PM or correct maintenance event this is the number of days since the PM was last performed or number of days since the work order was raised. For a meter based PM the field displays the number of meter units accumulated since the PM was last performed. Due: This field displays either the Due Date (for calendar PMs or deferred work orders) or the meter count at which the work is due (for meter PMs or work orders deferred by a meter value). End Item Due Count: The count at which the work is due at the end item level (top level asset). Deferrals: Checkbox which, if true, indicates that a work order has been deferred. Deferrals are perfomed in the Work Order Tracking (CM) application. Left: The number of days or meter units remaining before the work is due. Work Order: A work order number. Explanation of field values in the table detail: Active Date Reviewed: This checkbox indicates if the frequency information for the maintenance event needs to be reviewed. This checbox is generally set to false for PMs that were created automatically by the system. For example, if a new Master PM was made active and the system created PMs for the assets with the same CM Items as listed on the Master PM. In this scenario, it requires that a user must manually review the maintenance event and ensure that the point at which is next due is acccurate. If it is then the checkbox can be set to true and the record saved. If the checkbox is set to false the BDI will raise a ENR (Event Needs Review) problem code for the PM. This is considered to be an INVALID configuration as scheduled maintenance is active but not correctly initialised. The system will not automatically created work orders for PMs where the associated maintenance event is marked as needing review. Current Count: For meter based maintenance events, displays the current total for the meter. Last Date: Displays the last date that the PM was completed. Last Count: Displays the meter count at the date of last PM completion (relevant for meter based events only). Active Date: The date and time at which the maintenance event became active. Normally this would be the same as the date the PM was last completed. For corrective maintenance this is the report date of the work order. A further explanation of how this effects alert, warning and due date/count calculations is decribed in detail later in this topic. Alert Date: The Alert Date of the maintenance event. Applicable for calendar based PMs only. The BDI will generate a work order automatically when the alert date is reached or exceeded. An EBA (Event Beyond Alert) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Alert Date. Warning Date: The Warning Date of the maintenance event. Applicable for calendar based PMs only. An EBW (Event Beyong Warning) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Warning Date. Due Date: The Due Date of the maintenance event. Applicable for calendar based PMs only. An EBD (Event Beyond Due) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Due Date. Active Count: The meter total for the asset at the Active Date. See later in the topic for an explanation of the logic around meter calculations in relation to maintenance events. Alert Count: The Alert Count of the maintenance event. Applicable for meter based PMs only. The BDI will generate a work order automatically when the alert dcountate is reached or exceeded. An EBA (Event Beyond Alert) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Alert Count. Warning Count: The Warning Count of the maintenance event. Applicable for meter based PMs only. An EBW (Event Beyong Warning) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Warning Count. Due Count: The Due Count of the maintenance event. Applicable for meter based PMs only. An EBD (Event Beyond Due) BDI problem code is raised once a PM has reached or exceeded the Due Count.

Both the "Due Date" and/or "Due Count" for a Maintenance Event record is calculated based on the Active Date recorded on the maintenance event and the Frequency/Interval of the associated PM. These calculations are described below Calendar Frequencies: Due Date = (Active Date + Calendar Frequency) - Due Count Offset Note: The "Due Count Offset" is optional but can be used to adjust the Due Date in the case where the Active Date + Calendar Frequency does not give the desired due date value. When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute from Active: Alert Date = (Active Date + Alert Interval) - Due Count Offset Warning Date = (Active Date + Warning Interval) - Due Count Offset When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute Prior to Due: Alert Date = Due Date - Alert Interval Warning Date = Due Date - Warning Interval Meter Frequencies: The calculation for meter based maintenance events involves the use of the ACM calculated life algorithm. Due Count = (Active Count) + Meter Frequency) - Due Count Offset Where Active Count = The meter total derived by the calculated life algorithm for the asset at the Active Date. Note: The "Due Count Offset" can be used to adjust the Due Count in the case where the Active Count + Meter Frequency does not give the desired due count value. When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute from Active: Alert Count = (Active Count + Alert Interval) - Due Count Offset Warning Count = (Active Count + Warning Interval) - Due Count Offset When PM "Alert and Warning Interval State" = Absolute Prior to Due: Alert Count = Due Count - Alert Interval Warning Count = Due Count - Warning Interval

documents.t: The Modifcation Status tab displays information on which design changes, modifications or campaigns have been embodied (carried out) or are due for completion for a CM managed asset hierarchy.

The Modification Status tab displays the status of Technical Records which are active against the current configuration-managed asset. A number of options are provided to filter the table(s) displayed on the tab. When an option checkbox is changed the "Refresh View" button should be clicked to update the data within the tables: Option Description Include Children? When set to true, this checkbox causes a second Modification Status table to be displayed. The table list the modification status of Technical Records against the sub assembly assets within the main asset hierarchy. Fully Embodied? When set to true, the tables will display any Technical Records which have been fully embodied (complied with) for the asset(s) Active? When set to true, the tables will display any Technical Records are active and applicable to the asset(s) but have not yet been complied with. Partially Embodied? When set to true, the tables will display any Technical Records which are active but have only been partially emboded. This is a special status to indicate work may have been started against the asset but has not yet been fully embodied (eg a two part service bulletin). Not Applicable? When set to true, the table will display any Technical Records which are active against the asset but have been marked as not applicable. Each table provides details on the specific Technical Records which are active and applicable to the asset. It includes details of when and by whom the change was performed by.
This page gives an overview and explanation of the capability and logic used in Maximo Asset Configuration Manager (ACM) to manage asset install and removal transactions.

documents.t: The install/remove functionality, provided for configuration-managed assets, is designed in such a way as to record a complete history of the installation and removal history of configuration-managed assets. It is also designed in such a way as to provide the ability to perform retrospective or out of sequence transactions. The aim of this documentation is to provide users of ACM with guidance as to this logic, how the data is persisted and how it is presented to the user within the ACM interface. The installation and removal history of configuration-managed assets is persisted in the table: PLUSASAONFF Each individual PLUSASAONOFF record records either: A period of time where an asset was installed into a parent assembly. A period of time where an asset was NOT installed into a parent assembly. A period of time where a specific position within an asset assembly structure was empty. Due to the way this information is persisted within this table, the system provides the ability to view the sub assembly structure at any point in time (Referred to as the "As of Date") in the assets lifecycle. A list of the main attributes of the PLUSASAONOFF table is detailed below: Attribute Name Data Type Description ASSETID BIGINT The installed Asset identifier. For PLUSASASONOFF records representing periods where a position in a parent assembly was empty this value is NULL. PARENTASSETID BIGINT The Parent Asset identifier. For PLUSASASONOFF records representing periods where an Asset was not installed this value is NULL. ONTIME DATETIME The date and time at which either: 1. An asset was installed into a parent assembly. 2. The beginning of the period of time where an asset was NOT installed into a parent assembly. 3 The beginning of the period of time for which a position within a parent assembly was empty. The PLUSASAONOFF.ONTIME should be populated on all PLUSASAONOFF records. OFFTIME DATETIME The date and time at which either 1. An asset was removed from a parent assembly. 2. The end of the period of time where an asset was NOT installed into a parent assembly. 3 The end of the period of time for which a position within a parent assembly was empty. The PLUSASONOFF.OFFTIME maybe NULL and this represents the "current" data about the asset or position. LABEL UPPER The Label of the position POSITION UPPER The Position code of the position NAME UPPER The Build Item name of the position LCN UPPER The LCN of the position CURTOPASSET BIGINT The asset identifier of the asset at the top of the current assembly. NONTRACKED YORN =1 if the position is flagged as non-tracked in the Models Build Hierarchy. NONSERIALIZED YORN =1 if the position is flagged as non-serialized in the Models Build Hierarchy. SOFTWARE YORN =1 if the position is flagged as a software position in the Models Build Hierarchy. TYPE UPPER The Type of the transaction (described in detail below)

In order for the system to provide the ability to record installation and removal transactions out of chronological sequence a "Type" value is recorded on each PLUSASAONOFF record. This is used to signify additional information about the transaction for the purposes of transaction integrity. Four possible "Type" values exist: Type Value Description G (Gap) A PLUSASAONOFF record with a Type=G, represents either: 1. A period of time between 2 dates when a position is empty (PLUSASAONOFF.ASSETID IS NULL) or; 2. A period of time where a sub assembly asset is not installed (PLUSASAONOFF.PARENTASSETID IS NULL). If the Off Time is null on the record with Type=G this reflects that the position is currently empty or the asset is not currently installed. N (Valid On) Signifies that the date on which the asset was installed (PLUSASAONOFF.ONTIME) into a parent assembly is a confirmed date. I.e. An explicit installation transaction was carried out to install the asset into a parent assembly. If the the Type of the Transaction=N but the Off Date is populated then this "Off Date" value was assumed by the system. This assumption is based on the fact that no explicit removal transaction was recorded. This is considered by the system to be invalid configuration history (explained further below). F (Value Off) Signifies that a confirmed removal of an asset from a parent assembly took place at the Off Date but there was no corresponding confirmed installation of this asset into the parent assembly and position. In this situation the On Date and Time had to be assumed by the system (explained further below). B (Both N and F are valid) Signifies that Both the On Date and Off Dates and times were confirmed transactions. Invalid Configuration History Situations If the installation and removal of assets are recorded within the system in the same chronological order and with the same transaction dates as those with they were performed physically then the PLUSASAONOFF records would not normally require modification. However, in circumstances where a mistake is made or the chronology is wrongly reported or incomplete then the BDI may report a Problem Code of ISR (Invalid Installation and Removal History). This can happen under the following two conditions: TYPE = N AND OFFTIME IS NOT NULL: This indicates an "assumed" removal needed to be performed. In this situation, where an install of the asset is performed into one position without explicitly performing a removal of the asset from another (different) position. One scenario where this can occur is when a user installs an asset, which is already installed into another parent and position at the "As of Date", but the user fails to first remove the asset from its existing parent/position. To correct this a removal transaction must be performed for the asset with a transaction date that is after the "On Date" but on or before the assumed removal date. If the assumed removal date is correct then the user can confirm this by modifying the Off Date in the Position History tab and setting it back to the date and time of the removal then saving. TYPE = F: This indicates an Asset was removed from a parent assembly but there was no confirmed prior installation of the asset into the position within that parent assembly. One scenario where this may occur is when an asset is removed at one "As of Date" and then another removal is performed at an earlier "As of Date" (from the same parent and position). To correct this an installation transaction must be performed for the asset, into the relevant position, with a transaction data between the dates of the two removal (F) transactions.
The Assets (CM) application allows a user to understand the status of and perform actions against configuration-managed Assets.

The Assets (CM) application is a clone of the standard Maximo Assets application. It contains additional fields, tabs and actions so that the user can understand the status of configuration managed assets. It also provides additional actions so a user can update the as maintained configuration data of CM managed assets. Assets (CM) List Page The list page displays a list of Assets included CM managed and non-CM managed Assets. To display only CM managed assets the user can filter on the "CM Item" field with the "not null" filter value: "!=null" The page also displays an icon indicating the Configuration (BDI) Status for CM Managed Assets. The possible icon values are: Icon Status Description OK Configuration status is OK and no problems currently exist. INVALID A critical problem exists for the assets configuration that should be investigated and remedied. ALERT The asset has a configuration status that a user should be aware of but immediate action may not be necessary. UNKNOWNN The configuraiton status of the asset is unknown. This is used when no configuration status records exist for the asset Normally this is because the asset has not yet been validated by the BDI. Assets (CM) Main Page The main "Asset" page of the Assets (CM) application contains a number of addtional fields containing the CM related attributes of the Asset.
The Assets (CM) View tab is the main screen from which a user can understand the configuration status of a configuration managed asset

The "View" tab is used to understand the as maintained configuration data for a configuration managed asset. It is hidden (using Maximo conditional UI) for assets which are not configuration managed. The top section of the screen contains the following fields, buttons and UI components: Asset Hierarchy The Asset Hierarchy UI component provides a hierarchical view of a configuration managed asset assembly. It displays key information, taken from the corresponding build postions within the related Model, such as Label, Position, Position Name and LCN. In addition each node in the hiearchy displays information about the Asset installed into the position: Asset Number, Serial Number and CM Item. Clicking on the BDI Status icon at the far right of each node in the hierarchy opens the BDI Status dialog for the asset in the position. As of Date The "As of Date" field defaults to the current system date and time when the user enters the application. The user can change this date to a point in time in the past to understand what the configuration status of the Asset was at this point in time. When a user changes the "As of Date" field value, and tabs out of the field, the Asset Hierarchy will be updated to display the Asset Hierarchy as it was at this date and time. Now Button Clicking the "Now" button updates the "As of Date" field to the current system date and time. It then automatically refreshes the Asset Hierarchy view so that it displays the current as maintained configuration of the asset assembly. Perspective The Perspective field contains a list of Systems which have been defined in the associated Model. The default Perspective is the physical Asset Hierarchy corresponding to the main Build Hierarchy in the Model. Systems can be used to define functional system views within the Model to aid users in understanding which assets form part of particular functional systems within the Asset assembly.

Right clicking a node in the Asset Hierarchy opens a context menu with a list of actions that can be performed against the selected position. The actions provided by each item in the menu are listed below. Each action opens a dedicated dialog for the specific action: Action Description Install/Remove Asset Provides the ability to install / removal of a child asset from the selected position. It is used from installing removing assets from Sub Assembly positions or Installation Point positions. Switch Equipment Positions Provides the ability to "switch" multiple assets between positions within the current asset assembly. The positions must be created from the same Build Item in the Model to allow the switch to take place. Install/Remove Assets From Serialized Build Position Provides the ability to installed/remove assets ina multiple serialized quantity position. Non-Serialized Build Position Provides the ability to update the quantity of CM Items associated with a non-serialized build position. Change CM Item Provides the ability to change the CM Item associated with a CM Managed asset. Change Registration Provides the ability to change the Registration of a CM Managed asset. This action can only be performed against end item assets. Change Serial Provides the ability to change the Serial number of a CM Managed asset. CM Item Change History Displays the history of changes to the CM Item of a CM Managed Asset. Registration Change History Displays the history of changes to the Registration of a CM Managed End-Item Asset. Serial Change History Displays the history of changes to the Serial Number of a CM Managed Asset. View Configuration Change History Displays the history of changes to the Configuration of a CM Managed Asset End-Item Asset CM Rules Displays the CM Rule information for the selected position. BDI Status Opens the BDI Status dialog for the selected position.

A series of sub tabs is displayed at bottom of the Assets (CM) View tab. The information displayed in each tab relates to the node in the Asset Hierarchy that is currently selected. In addition the information displayed in the tab also reflects the current "As of Date" value.

The "Initial" tab displays the CONTINUOUS type meters (ASSETMETER records) associated with the CM Asset. Note that GAUGE and CHARACTERISTIC type meters are managed on the main "Meters" tab. Each Meter has to have an Initial Reading Date and Initial Count. These are used to initialise the point from which we wish to track the life of the asset within the Maximo system. All meter readings entered against the asset must have a Meter Reading Date later than the Initial Reading Date. The Initial Count should reflect the life of the meter at the Intial Reading Date. The Meter which is marked as the "Default" is used to calculate "TS Install" (Time Since Install) values displayed on the Parent, Child and Position History tabs. Explanation of Fields: "Current" : Displays the total for the Meter at the "As of Date". "Since" : Displays the number of meter units accumulated since the Initial Count (Since = Current - Initial Count). "Estimated?" : Indicates if the Intial Count for the Meter was estimated.

The "Direct" tab displays the CONTINUOUS type Meter Readings (METERREADING) that have been created directly against the asset selected in the Asset Hierarchy. Meter readings can be added, deleted or updated on this tab. Note that the meter reading date cannot be modified once a record is saved (only the meter value, either delta or actual depending on reading type). If a mistake is made with the reading date then the meter reading should be deleted and a new reading added with the correct date.

The "Summary" tab displays up to three rows for each continuous type meter for the selected asset. The "Type" for each row indicates what the count signifies: Initial Reading: The intial reading (taken from the ASSETMETER.PLUSANCHORCOUNT) for the asset. Direct: The total of the meter reading records created for the select asset. Indirect: The total number of meter units calculated for the asset based on readings against a higher assembly (during a period where the asset was installed into the higher assembly).

The "Maintenance Plan" tab displays any active Preventive Maintenance records for the selected asset. In addition it displays any open Work Orders (including both PM and corrective maintenance work orders). Together these records are termed "Maintenance Events". Due to the importance of the information contained within this tab the next topic is dedicated solely to this.

The BDI Queue Status application gives visibility on the BDI Queue and a history of the processing of Assets by the BDI. The application provides a list of all BDI Queue records, together with a status, how long they took to process and if there was an error. BDI Queue records are persisted in the database table: PLUSAANTRAN BDI Queue Status List Page BDI Queue Status Detail Page Information about errors are displayed in the the "stack trace" field which is displayed conditionally only when the status of the record is ERROR. This can be useful in helping to expedite the resolution of BDI errors when provided to a system administrator or as part of an IBM support case. BDI Queue Status Explanation Status Description PENDING The BDI queue record is awaiting processing. INPROGRESS The validation of the Asset by the BDI is inprogress. QUEUEUD The asset is currently being processed by the BDI but a configuration change has resulted in the need to process it again. COMPLETE Validation of the Asset by the BDI is complete. ERROR An error occurred during the validation of the asset. Consult a system administrator to report details of the error. If BDI queue records remain in a PENDING state for an unreasonable amount of time this could indicate a bottleneck in the queue processing component of the BDI application. The number of queue workers (threads) maybe increased or a dedicated BDI instance responsible for processing queue records can be created. The BDI Configuration topic gives more details on these options. Managing BDI End Points The BDI Queue Status Application contains an action "Manage BDI End Points" which opens a dialog containing the settings used to determine the service used for BDI API calls. A record is created in this table by default, on ACM installation, assuming there are no existing records in the table. If more than one BDI instance has been configured the dialog can be used to add these additional instances such that they will be candidates for BDI API requests. This can be useful if the number of simultaneous BDI requests, made from the BDI Status dialog by Maximo users, becomes too large for a single BDI instance to handle. A Maximo Item Set, Organization or Site can be associated with each End Point definition to cause requests for Assets, which match those values, to be routed to that instance. This can be useful for load balancing API requests. The port should always be configured as 9443 and the SSL toggle box set to "ON". The service host takes the form of: { instanceId }-{ workspaceId }-{ bdi-instance-name }.mas-{ instanceId }-manage.svc

The CM Item Master (CM) application provides the ability to define Configuration Managed Items. CM Items represent the components which make up a complex asset and, when applied to an Asset, is the primary attribute that differentiates a configuration-managed asset from a standard Maximo Asset. CM Items are used in a Model and form part of the engineering reference data used to define an as-designed configuration.

Field Name Description Example Value CM Item The name of the CM Item. The CM Item field is readonly and formed by concatentating the Part field with a space and the the Revision in square brackets. RTMT1481035 [A] Part A part number used to identify the component. RTMT1481035 Revision A revision of the part. Can be alphanumeric. A Dsecription A description of the part SALOON HVAC UNIT ASSEMBLY Vendor The Vendor of the part. HONEYWELL Item A link to a Rotating Item in the Item Master application.Typically the same value as the CM Item RTMT1481035[A] Category The type of part, for example HARDWARE, SOFTWARE HARDWARE Software Type The type of Software, If the CM Item has been categorised as software FLS Serial Format The format of the serial numbers associated with the CM Item. AANNN

The Serial Ranges table allows for the definition of one or more Serial Range Usable on Codes (UOC). The Serial Range UOC is a unique value, within the context of the CM Item, that is used to identify a range of serial numbers. The Serial Range UOC is then referenced within specific configuration rules within a Model for example to specifiy which positions or CM Items are valid for a specific range of end item serial numbers. Each Serial Range UOC has an associated Serial Range Expression which indicates the range of serial numbers to which the UOC is applied. The Serial Range Expression can be: A comma separated list of serial numbers: AA001, AA004, AA009 A range of serial numbers indicated by a double dot notation: A001..A100 Which indicates A001, A002, A003 etc all the way to A100 inclusive. A combination of both: A001, A003, A006..A009 Which indicates A001, A003, A006, A007, A008, A009

The Master PMs for CM Items table lists all those Master PMs which are related to the current CM Item. This relationship is normally established in the Master PM (CM) application. The system will, by default, create PMs for all Assets with the specified CM Item automatically. This occurs as part of the BDI validation of the Asset.

Add to Item Master The "Add to Item Master" action is used to create an Item Master record with the same name as the CM Item and establish a relationship between the two. The Item Master record will be automatically set to be Rotating=Y. When an Asset is created and the CM Item is specified the related Rotating Item Master record will also be applied to the Asset. The relationship between CM Item and Item Master is normally one-to-one.

The Master PM (CM) application enables the creation of master maintenance records which are linked to one or more CM Items. The application also provides additional functionality, for configuration-managed assets, over and above that provided by standard Maximo. Additional functionality provided in the Master PM (CM) application:

The CM Items table provides the ability to associate one or more CM Items with a Master PM. This enables the system to automatically create PMs from the Master PMs for configuration-managed assets with the CM Item listed on the Master PM. An action "Create Associated PMs for CM Items" is also provided to facilitate the immediate creation of PMs from the Master PM (for the applicable configuration-managed assets). PMs which are created automatically are marked as needing review to ensure the next date or meter count at which they will become due is accurate. A dedicated BDI Problem Code: ENR (Event Needs Review) is raised for PMs where this review needs to take place.

ACM introduces a Status field to the Master PM record (MASTERPM.PLUSASTATUS). When a new Master PM is created it has an initial status of DRAFT. This enables a user to setup the Master PM and configure it's various fields eg frequency criteria before making the Master PM Active. PMs cannot be created from the Master PM unless it is Active. In addition the system will not automatically create PMs from the Master PM (for applicable Assets) until the Master PM is made Active. ACM also introduces Revisioning functionality to the Master PM (CM) and PM (CM) applications. This operates in a similar way to revision functionality in other Maximo applications for example Job Plans. Master PM/PM Revision functionality is disabled in ACM by default. It must be enabled within the Organizations (CM) application. This is a system level setting and is contained within the CM Options section of the System Settings dialog. The option is a checbox labelled "Revision Control for Master PM / PM?". Once enabled, Master PM and PM records become read-only for configuration-managed assets. In order to make changes the record must be revised. This revision action creates a "copy" of the record with a pending revision (PNDREV) status. Once the necessary updates are made to this record it can be made active. The previous revision is placed into history with a status of REVISED. This enables full tracking of what has changed, when and by whom. The Build Data Interpreter will cause the update of the associated PMs automatically when it next validates the affected assets. Alternatively the action "Update Associated PMs?" will also trigger this immediately.

The Extendable checkbox, when set to true, indicates that the associated PMs as having the ability to be extended. A PM Extension is a controlled process to allow the Due date or Due Count to be extended for the next occurence of the PM. The PM Extension can be created in the PM (CM) application or the PM Extensions (CM) application. A workflow can be created against a PM Extension to create an approval process to activate the extension. PM Extensions are discussed in more detail in a separate topic.

The Master PM Actions provides the ability to define actions for the current "primary" PM which cause an action to be performed against a "secondary" Master PM/PM. These actions are automatically executed when specific events occur with the system such as work order completion or asset removal and install. The Master/PM actions are limited to primary / secondary PMs for the same CM Item or configuration-managed asset. That is to say, it is not possible to define an action on a primary PM, for a configuration-managed asset, which effects a secondary PM for a different configuration-managed asset. A list of the available action types, their associated effect and what triggers the action is detailed below: Action Type Triggered When Effect of Action ACTIVATE A work order generated from the primary PM is completed. The status of the secondary PM is changed to ACTIVE. COMPLETE A work order generated from the primary PM is completed. - The open maintenance event for the Secondary PM is marked as claimed and moved into history. - The next due date/count of the secondary PM is also reset based on the actual finish date of the primary PM work order. - If an open work order exists for the secondary PM its status is changed to COMPLETE CREATE WO A work order generated from the primary PM is completed. A work order is generated from the Secondary PM DEACTIVATE A work order generated from the primary PM is completed. The status of the secondary PM is changed to INACTIVE. OFF-ACTIVATE The asset associated with the primary PM is removed from a parent assembly. The status of the secondary PM is changed to ACTIVE. OFF-DEACTIVATE The asset associated with the primary PM is removed from a parent assembly. The status of the secondary PM is changed to INACTIVE. ON-ACTIVATE The asset associated with the primary PM is installed into a parent assembly. The status of the secondary PM is changed to ACTIVE. ON-DEACTIVATE The asset associated with the primary PM is installed into a parent assembly. The status of the secondary PM is changed to INACTIVE.
The "Advanced" tab provides a list of all of the Configuration Rules which exist for the current Model.

The advanced tab gives a consolidated list of the configuration rules which exist for the current Model. The normal mechanism to specify configuration rules is by the use of the various UI elements within the Build Hierarchy and Position Rules tab. The list of configuration rules can useful when trying to understand what rules exist as a whole, which revisions they relate to and also provides a mechanism to delete rules easily.

Indicates if the rule is positive or negative. Rules are normally negative to indicate that the Position, CM Item, Master PM etc are not applicably to a specific Configuration or position. Y or N Primary? All rules are considered to be primary. Y or N CSL Confguration Specification Language (CSL) statement with addition criteria which must be obeyed. This topic provides a more detailed explanation of how Models, Variants and Revisions relate to configuration-managed assets.

Every configuration managed asset, within Maximo, is evaluated (by the BDI and the system as a whole) in the context of it's current configuration attributes. The Models 'Core Concepts' and the Models(CM) application topics have described the concepts of Model, Variants and Revisions and provided an initial view on how these relate to CM assets. Model, Variant and Revision are the primary attributes that determine the Current Configuration of any configuration-managed asset. Here we go into more detail on how these primary configuration context attributes are determined for individual Asset records within Maximo. End Item assets End Item assets have these attributes explicitly recorded against them (using fields on the ASSET record, detailed in section Core Concepts - Assets). Non-End Item assets Non end item assets assume or inherit their current configuration based on a pre-determined priority order. That is to say, non-end item ASSET records do not explicitly reference a specific Model, Variant or Revision. This priority order, which determines a non-end item assets current configuration, is as follows: 1. End Item If the sub assembly asset has an ancestor which is an end item asset (asset above it in the asset hierarchy) that its current configuration is assumed/inherited from the first end item asset above it in the hierarchy. 2. Previous End Item If the sub assembly has been removed, from a parent end item asset, its current configuration is assumed based on where it was last installed. 3. New Asset Assemblies Record If the sub assembly has never been installed, as part of a parent end item assembly, its current configuration is taken from the New Asset Assemblies record it was created from. Initial Configuration If neither of the 3 situations above are applicable then the system may chose any Model, which references the Assets CM Item, as the context under which to validate the assets. This may be acceptable if the CM Item is only referenced in a single Model. If not then it is possible to apply an "Initial Configuration" explicitly to the non-end item asset. An Initial Configuration can be applied to a non-end item asset using the "Apply Configuration" action button located on the "Alternative Configuration" tab within the BDI Status dialog (found in the Assets (CM) application). This configuration will then be active against the asset until such time that the asset is installed into a higher end-item assembly. At this point this Initial Configuration is removed from the asset and point 1 above applies. BDI Status dialog showing how an Initial Configuration can be applied:

documents.t: The Build Hierarchy and Position Rules tab is used to define the physical structure of the Model and the configuration rules which form part of the allowed configuration.

The "Build Hierarchy and Position Rules" tab provides the user with the means to define the structure of a complex asset type. It allows the definition and visualisation of the parent/child relationship between the Build Positions. The image below shows an example Build Hierarchy, formed from the Models Build Items, for a Rapid Transit Metro Train: Build Hierarchy New positions can be added to the Model by right clicking a node and selecting the option "New Child" or "New Sibling". The dialog which is opened allows the user to specify the attributes for the new position: New Child

A more detailed description of the indicator values are detailed below S Build Item Each Build Position is constructed from a Build Item representing the sub assembly/component that must be tracked, managed and maintained BEARING ASSY Position A Position value which when combined with the Build Item and Label can be used by the user to easily identify the build position LEFT Indenture The level of indenture within the Build Hierarchy that the position resides (read only and system generated based on where the position is added) 2 LCN A Logistic Control Number (LCN) that is used by the system to uniquely identify a build position within the current Model. The LCN value is also used to determine the parent/child relationship between positions in the Build Hierarchy L0001

Positions can be freely added, moved (using the Move Up/Down and Push/Up down) or deleted from the Build Hierarchy in the situation where NO Assets have been created from the Model. Once Assets are created from the Model then restrictions are imposed in terms of the movement of Build Positions. This is enforced as the LCN value of a position is used, as part of the Assets as maintained configuration history, to record which assets have been installed into a position over the assets lifecycle. If assets have been created then it is possible to add new positions (with new, unique, unused LCN values) and also delete build positions. New in Maximo ACM 9.1.x In the situation where a build position is deleted a record is created to record that the associated LCN value has been previously used for this Model. When new Build Positions are added these previously used LCN values are by default "skipped" when generating the LCN value for the new position. Previously used LCN values can be viewed and managed using the action "View Used Build Position LCNs".
The Build Hierarchy and Position Rules tab is used to define configuration rules related to a Build Positions within the Model.

The information displayed in the "Position" sub tab relates to the selected build position within the asset hierarchy. Some of its features are to define different types of position, whether a position is mandatory for a Variant, or whether a position applies to a Variant of the Model.

Position Information The Position Information section gives general information about the Model. The fields within this section of the tab would not normally need to be modified. Position Quantities A standard position within a Model is referred to as a sub assembly position (Indicator=S). A standard sub assembly position provides the ability to install a child asset into the position within the associated asset hierarchy. In addition to this standard behaviour it is possible to also mark the sub assembly position as associated with a quantity. There are two distinct ways of defining this which have different behaviour when managing the assets associated with the position: Non-serialized If a position is flagged as a "Non-Serialized" position it is used to manage a quantity of non-serialized components. The Min and Max qty are validated by the BDI and if the quantity recorded against the position is outside of these limits a BDI problem code is raised against the asset position. The asset which is installed into the position can be considered as a "virtual" asset in that its only use is to be abe to record a quantity against it.
The Configurations tab of a Model is used to define Variants of the Model, Systems, Revisions and configure elements of BDI validation.

One of the main elements of a Model are its "Configurations". The primary configuration type for every model is referred to as a "Variant". When a Model is created a default "Base Variant" is created automatically. Additional variants may be added as children of the based variant. A Variant is a way to define and manage structured deviations from a base Model. The Variants can be used to specify differences in configuration that are known, planned, and allowed. Variants allow organizations to model different configurations of the same asset type without duplicating the entire Model, which keeps the model definitions reusable, clean, and scalable. The Variants are used as part of the defintion of specific types of "Configuration Rules" configured within the Model. For example specific Positions or CM Items within the Model can be marked as not applicable to a particluar Variant. In the screenshot shown below we see a 4 and 6 car variant of the Model: Rapid Transit Metro Train (RTMT). The specific positions within the train are marked as applicable (and mandatory) in relation to each of the 4 and 6 car variants (how this is done is described in the following sections). In order to create an Asset, from a specific Model and Variant, the Variant must be set to be non-abstract (Abstract checkbox=N), and its status must be ACTIVE. A description and comment can also be given to each Variant. To add a new Variant to the Model the user can right click an existing Variant and in the context menu displayed, chose the option "Add Child" (Highlighted in the screenshot above). This will open a dialog where details of the new Variant can be entered and confirmed.

The Revisions table allows for the definition of one or more revisions. A "BASE REVISION" is created automatically for each new Model. Explanation of Revisions The main impact of a Model Revision is its relationship to Congfiguration Rules. When a Configuration Rule is defined, it is done so in relation to a specific revision of the Model. A configuration rule will only be applied to an Asset if the Revision applied to the Asset is equal to or greater than the revision defined on the configuration rule record. For example if there are two Revisions defined for the Model: Revision 0 (BASE REVISION) and Revision 1 (FIRST REVISION) If a configuration rule is created with the "Revision Context" = 1 then this will only apply to Assets which also have Revision 1 or greater applied to them. Assets created from the Model which remain at Revision 0 will not be subject to the rule. Note that a later revision of the same rule can be created to override prior revisions of the same rule type for a specific build position. If the "Auto Upgrade?" checkbox is set to Y, for a Revision, then the BDI will automatically upgrade the associated assets to the latest revision which is set to auto-upgrade. BDI Map Codes The BDI Map Codes (sometimes referred to as Problem Codes) contains a list of every code which can be returned by the BDI to indicate a problem with the configuration of an Asset. A Map Code is a 3 letter code which indicates the type of problem together with a Description indicating under which conditions the code will be raised. Each code can be either active or inactive. If the code is marked as inactive, the BDI will skip executing the logic required to determine if the problem exists when validating the asset. In addition a Severity can be set for each Problem code. This will override the default Severity for that particular code. The default severity of each code is detailed in the BDI topic: Status and Problem Codes. Configuring Map Code Values The Map Code itself can be changed to a different 3 letter code if desired. Note that this change only effects the Model it is made against. To do this the following steps should be performed: In the Domains application, open the domain with name: PLUSABDICOND Add a new Synoym to the domain with the three letter code that should be used in replacement of the default code. The Internal Value sould be set to the original code. For example if the EBD code (Overdue Maintenance Event/PM) should be replaced with the code: PMD The Description is only used in the dispay of the Map Codes in the Models application: In the Models application delete the original code from the BDI Map Codes and save. Add a new row to the BDI Map Codes table and specify the replacement code, ensure the Active checkbox is set to true, and save again. The new replacement Map Code will then be active against the Assets where this Model is applied:
A model defines the engineering reference data and the allowable configuration for a type of complex asset.

As described in the Models core concept topic, a Model represents the as-designed configuration of a complex asset. It's used: To defined the allowable configuration for a type of complex asset and possibly variants of that asset type. As a template from which to build asset hierarchies used to maintain assets of the type described by the Model. By the BDI to validate the as maintained configuration of the asset against its allowable configuration described by the Model (and highlights problems).
The Models main page contains general information about the Model and fields which control it's definition.

The Build Items are a list of the main components (typically tracked and serialized) that are then used to create a build hierarchy representing the physical structure of the complex asset. They are related to one or more labels (typically one) and one or more CM Items which represent parts which provide the same fit, form and function of the component. Each Build Item records name must be unique within the Model it is contained within. When defining the Build Items and Build Hierarchy of a Model it is recommended that it is defined to the level at which it needs to be tracked and maintained in practice. Over-engineering an ACM model definition can lead to performance issues, user frustration, and increased maintenance overhead. The goal should be to model only what needs to be controlled or validated, and no more. Always try to balance precision with usability.

The Related Assets tab displays a list of the end-item Assets that the current Model is applied to.
The New Asset Assemblies (CM) application provides the ability to create Asset Hierarchies from a Model.

The New Asset Assemblies (NAA) application enables a user to create a CM managed asset hierarchy from a Model. The asset hierarchy created can be either: An entire assembly, starting with an end-item as the top level asset within the assembly. For example, a train set or train car. A partial asset assembly, where the top level asset corresponds to a position in the Models build Hierarchy at a level of indenture > 1. For example a bogie or wheelset within a train vehicle. The application enables the user to generate the data, using the Model as a template, from which the Asset records within Maximo will be created from. The basic flow of using the application is as follows: Create a new record. The user can enter a "New Asset" value which will be used as the Asset number of the top level asset. Alternatively the field (PLUSANEWASSET.ASSETNUM) can be configured to use the standard Asset autokey. Specify a "CM Item" corresponding to the top level asset of the new assembly. Select a Model/Configuration from the lookup on either field. The lookup will present a list of all values applicable for the CM Item including Model, Variant and Position. If the user is creating a partial asset assembly, and the CM Item is used in multiple positions, they should select the record in the lookup with the specific position corresponding to the assembly they wish to create. Enter other required information, for example: Serial, Registration, Asset Status. Specify a Location. If an Inventory Location is specified then the Asset will be added into the Storeroom on creation. Specify a Receipt Date and (optionally) a Date of Manufacture. Be aware that transactions, for example installation and removal of child assets can not be performed with an "As of Date" that is before the Receipt Date or Date of Manufacure (which ever is the earliest date). Enter Sub Assembly Prefixes. The Asset Prefix and Suffix values will be concatenated to form the asset number of each sub assembly asset. For example the Asset Prefix: "RTMT001-" and Suffix: "001" will result in sub assembly (child) assets being generated with the Asset numbers, RTMT001-001, RTMT001-002, RTM001-003 etc. This is useful when creating demo or test asset assemblies. Again the asset numbers for child assets (PLUSANEWSUB.ASSETNUM) can also be configured to use the standard Asset autokey. Enter Serial Prefix and Suffix values. The same logic is used to generate serial numbers for child assets as for the Asset numbers. Add the meters required to track life against the asset. The meters will be, by default, automatically added to all of child assets within the assembly. Note that the action "Create Meters from CM Build" will analyse all Master PMs linked to the CM Item specified. Any meters used on the Meter Frequency, of these related Master PMs, will then be added to the Meters table of the New Asset Assemblies record. Click the action "Create Sub Assemblies form CM Build". This will generate sub assembly information, based on the selected CM Item, Model, Variant and Position, from the related Model data and build hierarchy. On the "Sub Assembly Details" tab review the information for each of the sub assembly records to confirm accurate serial numbers, meter information etc. Change the status of the NAA record to ACTIVE (once the user has confirmed that all data is accurate). Click the "Create Asset" action to initiate the creation of the asset hierarchy. The user can choose to launch the action in the background and be notified by email on completion. This can be useful for large asset hierarchies where it may take some time to generate the entire asset hierarchy. Before the asset creation process is actioned the system will first verify that any Rotating Items linked to the asset or its children are valid within the Organization where the asset is to be created. The New Asset Assemblies information can be created or updated using the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF). An example is provided in MXLoader file is provided in the Loading Data topic. This can be useful to peform a bulk update of serial numbers, CM Items, meter information or related data before the asset creation action is executed. Using the Asset Autokey to generate Asset numbers In order to configure the system to generate Asset numbers, of new asset assembly records, using the standard Asset autokey a direct database update must be performed: UPDATE maxattribute SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWASSET' AND attributename='ASSETNUM'; UPDATE maxattributecfg SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWASSET' AND attributename='ASSETNUM'; UPDATE maxattribute SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWSUB' AND attributename='ASSETNUM'; UPDATE maxattributecfg SET autokeyname='ASSETNUM', canautonum=1, defaultvalue='&AUTOKEY&' WHERE objectname='PLUSANEWSUB' AND attributename='ASSETNUM'; Converting existing Assets into CM Managed Assets using New Asset Assemblies The New Asset Assemblies application can also be used to "convert" an existing Maximo asset hierarchy, of non-configuration managed assets, into one which is CM managed. It does this by updating the existing non-cm assets with the information necessary for the system to regard them as CM managed assets eg setting the CM Item on the ASSET record. In order to do carry out this conversion processing: The "Existing Asset" field should be populated with the existing non-cm managed asset number. Generate the sub assemblies using the "Create Sub Assemblies from CM Build" action. Update the asset number field on each sub assembly record to specify the existing non-cm managed asset number that will be placed in the corresponding position. Use the "Create Asset" action. The user will be presented with a dialog, listing each existing asset record, and ask the user to confirm the update to these existing asset records (to convert them into CM Managed assets). The conversion process will update the existing ASSET record to set the CM Item, Model, Variant and other CM managed data and attributes. If the asset does not have an parent it's parent will be updated to that corresponding to its position within the Build Hierarchy of the Model used. Meters will be added to the existing assets if they do not already exist. Adding Spares Parts, Condition Monitoring Points and Warranty Coming Soon.

This page gives details on advanced BDI configuration. This involves making direct modifications to the ManageWorkspace custom resource (CR) by an Open Shift administrator. Manage Custom Resource Settings Two BDI settings can be configured by updating (or patching) the "bdiConfigurations" section of the ManageWorkspace Custom Resource. Setting Description imagePullPolicy Determines when the BDI image will be retrieved from the IBM Entitled Registry. By default the value is: IfNotPresent. This setting is mainly used for internal development purposes. enableRoute: Determines whether an external Route is created, by the BDI entity manager, to the BDI OpenShift service. An external route can be useful for examining the BDI API documentation (Swagger docs) or making BDI API calls from an external system. A valid MAS 'x-access-token' cookie is required for external BDI requests. The default is for the Route to be enabled. Because the "bdiConfigurations" property of the ManageWorkspace custom resource is recorded in an Array it is recommended to update the yaml definition directly in the Open Shift console if modifying any of these additional properties. If an OC patch command is used to update the bdiConfigurations section of the ManageWorkspace Custom Resource then all of the properties in the bdiConfiguration array element must be specified. This is a limitation of the Kubernetes patch command. BDI Workload Customization The ManageWorkspace custom resource spec.components.acm can be updated to specify BDI container pod templates. For example to override the resources for the BDI Instance "bdi-1" the following yaml is specified: spec: bindings: jdbc: workspace-application components: acm: podTemplates: - containers: - name: bdiservice resources: limits: cpu: 3 memory: 8Gi requests: cpu: 1 memory: 1Gi name: bdi-1 replicas: 1 version: latest The following podTemplates fields are supported: replicas resources affinity tolerations securityContext nodeSelector topologySpreadConstraints

The ACM and Aviation Options parameters, specified within the BDI Instance configuration, are used to alter the functional behaviour of the BDI. Only one option is used and this is determined by which product is installed. The list of options available, and the effect they have on the BDI behaviour, is described in the table below. Those options that are only available in Maximo Aviation are indicated with a "Y" in the "Aviation Only" column. Option Value Description Aviation Only ECP Enables Event Calculation Persistence. The BDI will calculate and save values for the following fields on the PLUSALFEVENT table: P_LEFT, P_DUECOUNT, P_ENDITEMDUECOUNT, CALCDUEDATE, DATEDUECALC. P_LEFT = The number of days remaining until the due date or the number of meter units remaining until the due count. P_DUECOUNT = The due count at which the event (PM) will be due. P_ENDITEMDUECOUNT = The count at which the event (PM) will become due for the top level end item asset record. CALCDUEDATE = The estimated due date at which the event (PM) is due. This is equal to the due date for time based events. For meter based events this will be determined from the units remaining and the meter average of the asset. DUEDATECALC = The date and time when the PLUSALFEVENT record was last updated. N DCR Enables the Due Count Reached feature. When enabled in combination with the ECP option the BDI will "freeze" the PLUSALFEVENT.CALCDUEDATE for meter based events at the point the event became overdue. N MEL Enables MEL (Minimum Essential List) rules validation. A MEL problem is reported when the number of installed and operational items is less than the number required. The MEL is defined on the associated Model record. N MEL-RL MEL problems are reported by Label. Requires MEL option to be enabled. N MEL-RP MEL problems are reported by Position code. Requires MEL option to be enabled. N SRC Enables the evaluation and validation of Systems, Roles, and Capabilities. Roles and Capabilities are defined within the application "Asset/Aircraft Roles and Capabilities". N FLB Enables Flight Log Book validation (e.g. reporting AOG if Aicraft Status = GROUNDED) N OWO Enables monitoring for Orphan Work Orders; A BDI problem code "OWO" is reported when a PM is made INACTIVE and open work orders exist for the PM. N OWJ Enables monitoring for revised Job Plans; A BDI problem code "OWJ" is reported for open work orders where the associated Job Plan was revised post creation of the work order but before its completion. N OWT Enables monitoring for PMs. A BDI problem code "OWT" is reported for each open work order where the PM it was generated from was revised post its creation but before its completion. N TSX Enables persistence of Time Since Repair/Overhaul/Inspection and Life to Date Values. When enabled the BDI will calculate and persist life values in the PLUSAASSETTIMESINCE table for each configuration-managed asset/meter combination: SINCELASTREPAIR SINCELASTOVERHAUL SINCELASTINSPECT, SINCELASTINSPECT2 SINCEINSTALL LIFETODATE N XPM See detalied explanation below N -TRPNR Disables the Part Number Range capability associated with Technical Records. This option is mandatory when using the BDI with ACM. N PME Enables PM Extensions logic. Required when PM Extensions should be considered when evaluating PM Due Date/Counts. N SQP Enables the validation of Serialized Quantity Positions. Determines whether the BDI will report viloation of min/max quantity values when, a build position in a Model, is defined as a mutiple serialized quantity position. N SFT Enables Soft Task validation. When a PM is flagged as a Soft Task (PM.PLUSASOFTTASK=Y) then the BDI Problem Codes associated with PM Due, Warning and Alert intervals are altered to the following. SBA - Soft Task Beyond Alert. SBW = Soft Task Beyond Warning. SBD - Soft Task Beyond Due. The SBD code is treated as an Alert conditionby default. (Compared with INVALID for and overdue non-Soft Task.) N PMR When enabled the BDI will consider the "New Date" value specified on PM Forecast records when determining the PM Due Date. N OMP Enables monitoring for expired OMPs. A BDI probem code "OEX" is raised for active OMP records where the associated Expiry Date has been exceeded. (OMP = Operators Maintenance Plan). Y MPM Enables monitoring and validation of invalid mission flags on FLBs; MPM = Mission Profile-based Maintenance Y W&B Enables Weight and Balance validation. When enabled the BDI will report a "WAB" problem code when the latest Weight and Balance record for an Aircraft is flagged as being outside of the expected variance (as defined in the associated Aircraft Model). Y WOL Enables Whichever Occurs Later / Due on Last Deadline logic. When a Task Card is marked as "Due on Last Deadline?" (PM.PLUSADOLDEADLINE=Y) then it will only be considered overdue when all deadlines are exceeded (considers both Time and Meter Based frequencies/intervals) Y MPC Deprecated. Y SHL Enables Shelf Life logic. Y -UFI This is an Oracle DB Specific option. When specified, it will disable the use and automatic creation of functional indexes on the rowstamp column of tables which the BDI montiors. The BDI uses rowstamp values to monitor for changes within the Maximo database. Maximo on Oracle uses the datatype VARCHAR2 for rowstamp values which can makes comparisons of rowstamp values of different lengths uncertain. By default the BDI will create functional indexes of the form: (cast(rowstamp as number) when used with an Oracle DB. This enables queries which order on the rowstamp column to behave reliably. If this option is disabled the BDI will now perform casts on the rowstamp values but will instead restamp all rowstamp values within a monitored tables when it detects rowstamps of different lengths within the table.
