A single instance of the BDI is automatically deployed, with default settings, when Manage is activated with ACM in a MAS Workspace. Additional instances of the BDI can be configured if it is determined that a single instance is not validating all configuration managed assets frequently enough (this is typically a business decision). The individual configuration of each instance can be modified by clicking the "View" link. Before configuring additional instances it is advised that the various settings which control the BDIs operation are first analysed to determine if changes can be made to increase the throughput and alleviate bottlenecks. The user interface for the BDI settings, in the Manage Workspace activation page, is shown below:
Individual BDI Instance settings can be altered in the dialog shown below: A full description of each BDI Instance configuration setting is detailed below:

Name:​ A unique name for the BDI instance. It is recommended the default value is used. Max memory:​ The maximum Java heap memory that is assigned to the BDI instance. The BDI application is a web application deployed to Websphere Liberty. This setting is used to set the '-Xmx' JVM option used with the Liberty application server. The Advanced Configuration topic discusses using Pod Templates to provide addtional control over what resource limits are applied to the BDI container/pod. ACM and Aviation Options:​ The Aviation/ACM Options parameter is used to alter the functional behaviour of the BDI. Which one is used depends on which product is enabled. There a number of options which can be set which are detailed in a separate section.

Cache settings are used to control the memory usage of "cache" objects and the pool where they are taken from. A cache object is taken from a pool to service the request to validate an asset. It contains data cached from the Maximo database including Model, Asset and Preventive Maintenance data. Increasing the amount of memory used by a cache can improve performance but the trade off is increased memory consumption. Pool min:​ The minimum number of cache pool objects retained in the cache pool. It is initialised with this number when the BDI starts. Pool max:​ The maximum number of cache pool objects. For example if this is set to 8 the BDI instance will be able to service 8 simultaneous requests to validate an asset record. If additional requests are made while all cache pool objects are in use then the request will wait a number of milliseconds before retrying. The pool max should be >= (monitor.threads + vrex.workers + 1) to allow for enough cache objects to service requests from these processes simultaneously (detailed below). Pages and Assets per Page:​ These parameters can be used to tune the memory usage vs. the operational performance of the BDI. The default settings of 256 and 512 is generally suitable for a wide range of setups. This value means that each BDI cache pool object (used to service BDI requests) can “use” (i.e. hold in memory) a maximum of 256 pages (known as the “Cache Block Limit”) and each page can contain a maximum of 512 Maximo assets (known as the “Cache Block Size”) to give a total of 131072 assets. AV Mem Mode:​ The "AV Mem Mode" is used to control the number of meter readings and PM records which can be cached in memory.

The Queue Monitor or "Monitor" settings are used to control if, and how often, the BDI polls the BDI queue table (PLUSAANTRAN) looking for assets to validate. There is a separate configuration setting (described below) which determines the SQL executed to identify the pending records awaiting processing. Enabled:​ Determines if the Monitor process is enabled. Threads:​ The maximum number of assets in the queue which will be processed in parallel. Increasing this setting will mean more queued records can be processed simultaneously but will increase CPU load. Pulse seconds:​ How often the BDI will poll the BDI queue table looking for assets to validate. Clean Up Days:​ The number of days before completed BDI Queue records (those with a status of COMPLETE or ERROR) will be automatically deleted.

The "VREX" process is used to process configuration managed assets on a fixed schedule in the background. This ensures that all configuration managed assets are validated regularly (how often is typically a business decision). Enabled:​ Determines if the VREX process is enabled. Workers:​ Controls the number of Assets validated in parallel by the VREX process. Run on Start:​ Controls whether the VREX process is executed immediately when the BDI pod is started. Pulse Minutes:​ Controls how often the VREX process is executed. The default is every 180 minutes (3 hours). Start Time:​ Instead of executing the VREX process every x minutes the start time parameter can be used to specify a time of day at which the VREX process should be executed. This overrides the Pulse Minutes parameter.

The async job settings control the behaviour of when and how MAXASYNCJOB records are removed from the system. Delete On Start-up:​ This parameter controls whether the completed MAXASYNCJOB records are deleted when the BDI is started. Retention Days:​ The number of days which completed MAXASYNCJOB records, created by the BDI, are retained before being automatically deleted.

Log Level:​ Controls the logging verbosity of the BDI. A change to this value is deployed automatically without requiring the restart of the BDI pod. Select:​ The Select parameter is a series of SQL statements in an XML format. It is used to control which records the VREX and Monitor processes identify for processing. It contains DB specific sql which determines: The end items which will be validated by the VREX process: <end-item-select-{dbtype}> The non-end items which will be validated by the VREX process: <non-end-item-select-{dbtype}> The BDI queue records waiting for processing: <service-monitor-select> The Assets the BDI will consider for inclusion in its cache: <cache-select> The Master PM records the BDI will consider as part of validating an asset: <masterpm-select>

When an Asset is validated by the BDI it may need to perform an action that depends on the configuration status of the Asset. The BDI will create Asynchronous Jobs to perform these actions. These jobs are processed by a Maximo Crontask. As the BDI is a separate application to Manage it is unable to access the Maximo code directly. In order to invoke the necessary business logic it will create asynchronous jobs (MAXASYNCJOB) to perform the required action. A typical example of this is the generation of a PM Work Order. As these jobs are processed asynchronously, the overall time needed to validate the Asset is reduced. The asynchronous jobs, created by the BDI, are processed by Crontask instances within the Maximo Manage application. The Crontask responsible for the processing of Asynchronous Jobs by the BDI is named: PlusABDIAsyncImmediateJobCron By default, there is a single crontask instance per job type that the BDI may create. The type of job an instance is responsible for processing is controlled by the "jobnames" parameter. Additional Cron Task instances can be created if there is a bottleneck in the processing of jobs of a particular type. Additionally Cron Tasks instances which are responsible for jobs which may not be created, due to the way the customer uses the product, may be deactivated.

The table below lists the types of Jobs that the BDI may create, depending on the configuration status of the Asset: Job Name Description Class Name PLUSABDI_CREATEPM Creates missing PMs from Master PMs based on applicability. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusACreateMissingPMAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_REVISEPM Updates an associated PM from the Master PM. If revsion functionality is enabled then revise the PM. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusARevisePMAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_CHGPMSTATUS Changes the status of the PM to that of the supplied parameter. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusAChangePMStatusAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_GENERATEPMWO Generates a work order for the specified PM. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusAGeneratePMWOAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_CREATESEIWO Creates a work order for and empty mandatory position. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusACreateSEIWOAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_CREATETRPM Creates missing PMs for Technical Records based on applicability. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusACreateMissingTRPMAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_CREATEMELWO Creates a work order for a Mininum Equipment List (MEL) condition. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusACreateMELWOAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_CHGFLBDISCSTATUS Changes the status of an Flight Log Book (FLB) discrepancy record (PLUSALFLBDISCREPANCY) psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusAChangeFLBDiscrepancyStatusAsyncJobHandler PLUSABDI_CHGWOSTATUS Changes the status of a Work Order. psdi.plusa.app.asset.virtual.asyncjobs.PlusAChangeWOStatusAsyncJobHandler

A Grafana Dashboard will be automatically deployed as part of ACM to enable monitoring of key BDI metrics. Overview When ACM is installed a dedicated BDI Grafana Dashboard will be automatically deployed. This assumes that Grafana is installed and configured on the Open Shift cluster. The MAS Ansible Devops collection contains a role to automate the deployment of Grafana.

The key metrics displayed in the dashboard are described below: Validation Queue Back Log: Displays the number of records in the BDI queue with a status of PENDING or QUEUED. A sustained large number indicates that the monitor process may be failing to keep up with the rate at which records are being placed into the queue by the system. Solutions to this maybe increasing the number of monitor threads or configuring additional BDI instances. API Validation Requests/min: The number of requests to validate an asset per minute received by the BDI API. The API requests would normally come from usage of the Validate Configuration button in the BDI Status dialog. BDI DB Connections: Displays the current number of open database connections created by the BDI. The BDI operates a JDBC connection pool where new connections are opened depending on simultaneous validation request. Connections which are open but have not been used in the last 5 minutes will be automatically closed. VM Status Pool Size: Displays the current number of cache objects in the cache pool used to service BDI requests. Heap Memory Usage: Displays Java Heap memory usage for all BDI pods. CPU Usage: Displays CPU usage for all BDI pods. Async DB Writer Queue Size: Displays the number of asynchronous database updates waiting for execution. Certain database updates performed by the BDI are performed asynchronously to optimize performance. If the number of records displayed here is consistently high and never falls to zero it could indicate a requirement for additional BDI instances Async Job Writer Queue Size: Displays the number of asynchronous jobs waiting to be executed for insertion into the Maximo database. If the number of records displayed here is consistently high and never falls to zero it could indicate a requirement for additional BDI instances.

This page contains a list of status and problem codes which can be returned by the BDI BDI Status Codes Status Description OK The Asset has no problems with its configuation or overdue maintenance. ALERT The Asset has one or more problems which the user should be aware of but the asset can continue to operate safely. For example, maintenance that is approaching a deadline. INVALID The Asset has one or more serious issues that should be investigated immediately. For example, This could be invalid parts installed, missing mandatory parts or overdue maintenance. AOG A special status which indicates a Flight Log Book exists for the Asset with an Aircraft status of GROUNDED. BDI Problem Codes The RED codes are serious problems which will result in the Assets configuration status being set to “INVALID”. The AMBER codes are less serious problems that may affect the operation of the Asset. This includes approaching maintenance tasks that will require action in the short term. The Asset’s status will be “ALERT”. The GREEN codes are created when the BDI is validating an “alternative configuration”. When the BDI is run in “update” mode, these problems are automatically corrected (e.g. Maintenance Events and Build Positions are created or removed). The BLUE codes are for information only. INVALID Codes Problem Code Problem Description BMR Invalid Position The Build Position is invalid due to applicability rules or Technical Publications. or The non-serialized position has a negative quantity, or a quantity less than the minimum allowable quantity, or a quantity exceeding the maximum allowable quantity. AOG Aircraft on Ground The active FLB (Flight Logbook) for the aircraft has a status of GROUNDED or UNKNOWN, or there is an open Ticket with status of AOG. EMR Invalid Position for the EISUOC The Build Position is invalid due to end item serial effectivity rules (i.e. regarding the Build Position’s applicability to the End Item Serial Usable On Code). SIR Invalid Part Number Installed The CM Item installed in the Build Position is invalid due to applicability rules or Technical Publications SSR Duplicate Part and Serial Number. The Asset installed into the position has the same CM Item and Serial Number as another Asset within the system. ISR Invalid Install / Remove History An overlapping Install-Remove history was found for the Asset or a Position on the Asset. SMM Missing Mandatory Position The mandatory Build Position is missing. If the BDI is running in update mode, the position will be created but will then have an SEI status [Empty Mandatory Position]. SEI Empty Mandatory Position The mandatory Build Position is empty. SSU Serialized Quantity Below Minimum The number of assets installed into a position which is designated as a mulitple serialized quantity position is below the minimum quantity defined in the associated Model and build position. SSO Serialized Quantity Above Maximum The number of assets installed into a position which is designated as a serialized quantity position is aboe the maximum quantity defined in the associated Model and build position. EIR Invalid Part Number Installed for the EISUOC The CM Item of the asset installed in the Build Position is invalid due to end item serial effectivity rules (i.e. regarding the CM Item’s applicability to the End Item Serial Usable On Code). XDP Invalid Part Installed The Part Number installed in the Build Position is invalid due to a cross-structural or higher-part applicability rule. ENR Event Needs Review The Maintenance Event (PM) created by the BDI needs to be reviewed for validity of the Active Date. EBD Event Beyond Due The open Maintenance Event (PM) has exceeded its Due date or Meter Reading. MEL Minimum Equipment List An End Item has a MEL rule that has not been satisfied The BDI will generate a MEL BDI code and a MEL work order when: The BDI Options setting contains the value “MEL”. The asset is an end item. The asset’s Model has its MEL flag set to true. There is a MEL rule associated with the assets’s Model that has not been satisfied. ALERT Codes Problem Code Problem Description EBA Event Beyond Alert The open Maintenance Event (PM) has exceeded its Alert Date or Meter Reading. EBW Event Beyond Warning The open Maintenance Event has exceeded its Warning Date or Meter Reading. NAD Non-AOG Discrepancy An active FLB for the aircraft has a status of LRTS (Limited Release to Service) or DRTA (Deferred Release to Service), or there is an open Ticket with a non-AOG status. SED Empty Mandatory Deferred Position The mandatory Build Position is empty but has an associated Deferred Work Order. OWO Open Work Order Exists where the associated PM is INACTIVE An open work order exists where the associated PM has been made INACTIVE. OWJ Open Work Order Exists where the Job Plan applied to it has been revised. An open work order exists where the Job Plan applied to it has subsequently been revised. OWT Open Work Order Exists where the PM from which it was generated has been revised. An open work order exists where the PM from which it was generated has subsequently been revised. SBA Soft Task/PM Beyond Alert The active PM with the "Soft Task" checkbox set to true has exceeded its Alert Date or Meter Reading. SBW Soft Task/PM Beyond Warning or Due The active PM with the "Soft Task" checkbox set to true has exceeded its Warning or Due Date or Meter Reading. INFORMATION Codes Problem Code Problem Description EMC Event Missing A required Maintenance Event (PM) is missing. If the BDI is running in update mode, the PM will be created. EID Extra Event The Maintenance Event (PM) is not applicable. If the BDI is running in update mode, the Maintenance Event will be removed (if there is no associated Work Order). and the PM will be made INACTIVE. BMD Empty Extra Position An empty Build Position is invalid due to applicability rules or Technical Publications. If the BDI is running in Update mode, this Build Position will be removed EMR Invalid Position for the EISUOC The empty Build Position is invalid due to end item serial effectivity rules (i.e. regarding the Build Position’s applicability to the End Item Serial Usable On Code). If the BDI is running in Update mode, this Build Position will be removed. SMO Missing Optional Position An optional Build Position that is required by the CM rules is missing. If the BDI is running in mode, the Build Position will be created.
The Alternative Configuration tab provides the ability to validate and apply an alternative configuration to an Asset.

The Alternative Configuration tab lists all of the Model/Configurations which are candidates to be applied to the current asset. It gives the user the ability to validate a different configuration by using the “selected” checkboxes and the "Validate Configuration" button. The ‘Status for Selected Configuration’ and Problems table will then display data relevant to the configuration that was selected and validated. The user can also change the configuration(s) applied to the asset by clicking the “Apply Configuration” button. The selected configurations will then be applied resulting in a change to the current configuration of the Asset. In the screenshot shown, the current configuration of the train is: RTMT-4 (4 Car Consist). The user has chosen to validate the Asset against the RTMT-6 (6 Car Consist). The Problems table displays that there are 3 problems: SMM (Missing Mandatory Position): TRAILER CAR in position 4 is not installed. SMM (Missing Mandatory Position): MOTOR POWER CAR in position 5 is not installed. EBD (Overdue Maintenance): A PM deadline has been exceeded. If the user chooses to apply the RTMT-6 Variant to the Asset they will need to install the two missing cars and complete the overdue maintenance in order to reach a valid (OK) configuration status. The empty positions for the two missing cars will be created automatically when the RtMT-6 variant is applied.

In addition to changing the configuration (Variant) applied to an Asset it is also possible to change the Model. In order to do this the CM Item associated with the end-item asset must first be changed to that of the target Model. The Assets (CM) application provides an action "Change CM Item" to make this change. Once the CM Item is changed the "Configurations" window will display the Model associated with the new CM Item and the user can choose to apply a new Model and associated Variant configuration.

documents.t: The BDI Actions tab displays a list of the asynchronous jobs that have been created by the BDI for the current Asset or its children. Part of the BDIs repsonsibility is to perform specific actions as a result of the configuration status of an Asset. Examples include genererating work orders at a pre-determined alert interval or creating a new PM from a Master PM. The mechanism used to perform these actions is by the use of "Asynchronous Jobs". The asynchronous job records are stored in the MAXASYNCJOB table and are processed by a dedicated group of Maximo Cron Tasks. The BDI Actions tab lists the recent jobs, created by the BDI, for the current Asset. Each job has: Job Name + Description: The Job name indicates the type of Job and the description provides more context. A Status and Status Date indicating when the current status of the Job and when the status was last updated. Expanding the table row gives additional information about the processing of the job. Job Messages: Details the progress of the processing of the job. Job Parameters: List the parameters necessary to support the processing of the job.

The BDI Actions / Asynchronous Jobs have the following 4 possible status values: Submit Description SUBMIT Job was created by the BDI and is awaiting processing. INPROGRESS Job is currently being processed by a Maximo BDI Crontask instance. SUBMIT Job has finished processing successfully. ERROR An error was encountered during processing of the job. Consult the Job messages for further information. A full list of Asynchronous Jobs that can be created by the BDI is provided in a separate section.

The "Current Configuration" tab is used to understand details on the current configuration status of a configuration-managed asset. The tab provides an overall configuration status as well as information on what problems currently exist for the asset.
The "Asset Configurations" table displays the current Model and Configuration(s) which are applied to the Asset.

The "Configuration Status" section displays: Status - The overall Configuration Status. Status Date - The date and time the configuration status was assigned it's current value. Last Updated - When the BDI last validated the asset. Revision - The current revision of the Model applied to the Asset. Hold Revison - Can be used to ensure a specific revision of the Model is applied to the asset (not auto-upgraded to the latest active revision) The Status has four possible values: Status Description OK The Asset has no problems with its configuation or overdue maintenance. ALERT The Asset has one or more problems which the user should be aware of but the asset can continue to operate safely. For example, maintenance that is approaching a deadline. INVALID The Asset has one or more serious issues that should be investigated immediately. For example, This could be invalid parts installed, missing mandatory parts or overdue maintenance. AOG A special status which indicates a Flight Log Book exists for the Asset with an Aircraft status of GROUNDED.

The Configuration Actions section provides the ability to send a request to the BDI to validate the Asset. This can be done by clicking the "Validate Configuration" button. The request can be launched in the background and an email notification can be sent to the user once the request is complete.

The bottom of the tab lists the problems, determined by the BDI, which currently affect the Asset. A Problem consists of: Problem Code: A 3 character code which indicates the type of Problem. Asset Information: Information on what Asset is affected by the problem including Asset number, CM Item Serial Number, Label, Position and Name. Severity: The severity of the problem. Narrative: A textual description of the Problem. PM/Work Order number: Populated for those problems which result from planned or corrective maintainance.

The BDI Status dialog enables a user to view details on the status of a configuration managed asset. In addition it can be used to: Make a synchronous call to the BDI to validate the asset and update its configuration status. Validate an alternate configuration to undertand what problems may result in changing an assets configuration. Change the configuration of an Asset by changing it's Model and/or Variant or applying a Role. View information about Asynchronous Jobs created by the BDI to perform actions against the Asset such as generating work orders. Details on the three tabs which make up the BDI Status dialog can be found in the other pages of this section. The BDI status dialog is accessible in the Assets (CM) application. It can be opened by right clicking a node in the Asset Hierarchy and clicking the option ‘BDI Status’ in the context menu (as shown below).

Specific user actions and events within the system will cause the BDI to validate configuration-managed Asset records asynchronously in the background. This is accomplished by the addition of a "PENDING" record to the BDI Queue table (PLUSAANTRAN). These records are processed by the "Monitor" component of the BDI application. The specific list of events which cause this to occur are as follows: Application Action / Event Assets (CM) Modifying an ASSETMETER record on the "Initial Meter Value" tab Assets (CM) New/Update/Delete of Meter Reading on the "New Meter Entry" ta Assets (CM) Work Order Tracking Install/Remove of sub assembly assets Assets (CM) Modification of a Maintenance Event record (PLUSALFEVENT) eg. modifying Active Date or changing value of Active Date Reviewed flag Assets (CM) Modification of data on the Position History tabs Assets (CM) Reset of Time Since related information Assets (CM) Change of Asset serial number Assets (CM) Change of Asset Part Number / CM Item New Asset Assemblies (CM) Creation of new Asset Flight Log Book (CM) Change of Aircraft status. Eg. RTS -> GROUNDED Technical Records (CM) Activation of Technical Record (All assets effected by TR) Work Order Tracking (CM) Change of WO status

Asset records form the basis of the as built and as maintained (operational) configuration data. They are used to manage and maintain the configuration of the asset over the course of its operational life time. Configuration managed assets are distinguished from standard Maximo (non-CM) assets by their association with a CM Item (and by extension a Model). CM assets also behave and are treated differently to non-CM assets, for example: Configuration managed assets are validated by the Build Data Interepeter (BDI) whereas non-CM Assets are not. Continuous type meter readings are recorded and calculated differently for CM Assets (covered in detail in the Meters section of this documentation). PM records for CM Assets are treated differentlty to those of non-CM assets.

Configuration managed assets can be further categorised as End Items or Non-End Items. The key distinction is that an end item asset is one created from the top-level postion within a model. This could be a parent model, such as an aicraft or train set, or an "installable" (sometimes referred to as a sub model) representing a major assembly that could be used in multiple positions eg. an engine or train car. Conversely a non-end item is one created from a child build position in a model.

CM Managed Assets have a number of other additional data attributes to that of standard Maximo Assets. The primary ones of interest are detailed below: Attribute Name Type End-Item / CM Assets Description PLUSACATID BIGINT All The unique id of the associated CM Item (PLUSACACAT). PLUSAMODELID BIGINT End-Item The unique id of the associated Model (PLUSACMODEL). PLUSACONFIGID BIGINT End-Item The unique id of the associated Variant (Primary) Configuration (PLUSACMCONFIG). PLUSAREVISIONID BIGINT End-Item The unique id of the Revision of the Model applied to the asset (PLUSACMREVISION). PLUSAREG UPPER End-Item The current Registration value for the asset. PLUSAMNFCTRDATE DATETIME All The date of manufacture of the asset. PLUSARCPTDATE DATETIME All the date of receipt of the asset into the system. Assets with an associated Model (ASSET.PLUSAMODELID IS NOT NULL) are considered by the system to be End Items.

Object Name End-Item or All CM Assets Description PLUSASAEIREG End-Item Registration Change History PLUSASAEICONFIG End-Item Configuration Change History PLUSASAASSETCAT All CM Item Change History PLUSASAASSETSN All Serial Number Change History PLUSASAONOFF All Parent/Child History over time (Discussed in depth in a separate section)

documents.t: The Build Data Interpreter (BDI) is a central and critical component of the Maximo Asset Configuration Manage solution. It is deployed automatically, as a separate application within the Manage namespace, when ACM is is activated as a component of Manage. It is responsible for verifying and ensuring the compliance of operational modifications to configuration-managed (CM) assets in accordance with the reference data and configuration rules defined within an associated model and its related maintenance plans. The BDI can be executed manually for a specific CM managed asset hierarchy, using the BDI Status dialog within the Assets (CM) application. The BDI also validates CM assets in the asynchronously in background in one of two ways: On a time-based schedule (by default every 3 hours) On an adhoc bases when when particular transactions, which may effect the configuration status of the asset, are executed by a user of the system or via an integration process.

Examines configuration-managed assets on a position-by-position basis, ascertaining their adherence to the configuration rules defined in the associated Model. Provides a comprehensive status for an asset, which can be viewed in the BDI Status dialog, and highlights non-conformity by reporting problem codes with corresponding details. Assesses the maintenance program for an asset and triggers the creation of work orders at a pre-determined alert threshold. An indepth description of the BDI, it's operation and configuration is provided in a dedicated section. Thes Assets (CM) application topic also goes into detail on how the BDI status for an Asset is reported.
A database function is provided, as part of the Asset Configuration Manager installation, which can be used for reporting purposes.

This database function is named: CALCLIFE The function accepts 4 parameters: Parameter Description ASSETID The Asset identifier (ASSET.ASSETID). SITEID The Site in which the asset resides (ASSET.SITEID). METERNAME The continuous meter name for which the meter total should be calculated. ASOFATE The date for which the the meter total should be calculated. When the current meter totals for many CM assets are required for a report it is preferrable to use the values persisted in the table: PLUSAASSETTIMESINCE This is because using the CALCLIFE database function has a performance overhead for many repeated calls. See next section for details of this table.

This page gives an example of how asset meter readings are used and how meter totals are calculated for configuration-managed assets. It demonstrates how meter readings entered against a parent assembly are considered along with the configuration history of the child asset. It also gives an intitial insight into how these totals are considered as part of the maintenance plan for components. Let's take an example for a Train: The train consists of a number of cars, the first of which is the Driver Motor Power Car. Within the car are two Motor Bogies which form part of the propulsion system for the train. The number of kilometers travelled is recorded against the top level train asset using the "ODOM-KM" continuous meter. Intial Tab​ Figure 1. Shows the "Initial" tab with the Train asset selected in the Asset Hierarchy view within the "Assets (CM)" application. We can see that an initial count of 4500 KM has been recorded against the train. The initial count is used to provide a baseline as to the life of the asset when it begins being managed in the Maximo system. The "Since" value shows that a further 3000 KM have been recorded against the train since it began operation. Figure 1. Direct Tab​ Figure 2. Shows three meter readings that have been entered against the same train asset. The readings are of type "DELTA" and the sum of these readings plus the Initial Count gives the total KM value of 7500 for the train. Figure 2. Summary Tab​ Figure 3. Shows the "Summary" tab for the train asset. This provides a summary of the meter readings entered against the asset (Direct) and the initial reading. For child assets this summary may also show an "indirect" row. This provides a total for the meter units inherited based on where the asset has been installed throughout its life. Figure 3. Inherited Readings​ If we now look at the same information for a Motor Bogie asset installed into the first position in the Drivers Motor Power Car: Figure 4. Shows the Initial tab for the Motor Bogie. We can see that the Motor Bogie has a different Intial Count (5000) to that of the train it is installed into. We can also see that it has an additional 9000 KMs that have been calculated for the Bogie to give a grand total of 14000 KMs. Figure 4. Figure 5. Shows the Summary Tab for the Motor Bogie. This time we see three rows: The Initial Reading Count of 5000 A Direct Count of 0 (as no meter readings are entered directly against the bogie) An Indirect Count of 9000 indicating 9000 KM have been calcualted based on where the bogie has been installed over the course of its life. Figure 5. But where did the 9000 KM come from? We demonstrated earlier how 3000 KM had been recorded against the train asset but this leaves a short fall of 6000. Figure 6. Shows the "Parent History" tab for the Motor Bogie. Here we can see where the Bogie has bee installed over the course of its life. We can see the On and Off Dates of when it was installed and removed together with a "TS Install". This "Time Since Install" gives a total value accumulated while the bogie was installed into a different train. In this example the Bogie was installed in a different train (TRAIN B) between the dates 3 April 2024 and 8 May 2025. It's while installed in this second train that a total of 9000 KM was recorded against the train. Figure 6.
Asset Configuration Manager provides the ability to calculate dynamic meter totals based on a formula. Further details and examples coming soon

Continuous Meters for configuration-managed (CM) assets operate in a different way to that of standard (non-cm) assets. This section discusses this important distinction in depth as it is an often misunderstood area. This topic is specific to Meters with a maximo meter type of CONTINUOUS. GAUGE and CHARACTERISTIC meters are treated and behave in the same way as standard Maximo Manage.

One of the key features of Maximo Asset Configuration Manager (ACM) is its ability to dynamically calculate the life (meter totals) of an asset at any point over the course of its life. Meter values can be derived and viewed for any point in time in the history of the assets life cycle. This "active life cycle accounting" provides improved compliance for regulated industries, while helping to increase reliability and accountability. The life of an asset, at a specific "As of Date" is calculated dynamically (at run time) using a dedicated algorithm which considers: The configuration history of an asset. Ie where it has been installed and between what dates. The information is recorded in the PLUSASAONOFF table. The meter readings entered against the asset directly and also any at a higher level within the asset hierarchy (for the dates in which the asset was installed). These are recorded in the METERREADING table. The Initial Reading Date and Initial Count. These are used to set an initial total for the meter at the date specified. This information is stored on the Asset Meter record in the fields: ASSETMETER.PLUSAANCHORDATE and ASSETMETER.PLUSAANCHORCOUNT. This means that meter readings can be entered against any asset within a complex configuration managed structure and these readings will be automatically "inherited" by all sub-assembly (child) assets, depending on the configuration history. The use of this dynamic meter calculation algorithm: Negates the need for an Asset "Rolldown" to child assets and duplication of meter readings. Means Any historical changes to the configuration of an asset or the creation, update or deletion of meter reading records will be immediately reflected on the asset and considered by associated maintenance plans when determining when they are next due.

It is important to ensure that the ASSETMETER.ROLLDOWNSOURCE is set to NONE for CM Assets. This should happen automatically for CM assets created through the application. Special care should be taken when loading datathrough the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF) that this is not value is not overridden. Dute to the dynamic life algorithm, meter readings should not be loaded against parent and child assets, either through the UI or and integration. This will result in an incorrect calculation for child assets.

Due to the dynamic way that meter totals are calculated with ACM, the ASSETMETER table for child assets will not persist an accurate LIFETODATE or SINCELAST% values. The ASSETMETER table will only reflect the "direct" readings which have been entered against the child asset. Any "indirect" readings, Ie. those readings inherited from a meter entry against a parent assembly are not recorded in the ASSETMETER table for a sub-assembly or child asset. To provide an alternative to this an additional table is provided and automatically updated for configuration-managed assets:

The PLUSAASSETTIMESINCE table records the current meter totals for a CM asset and its related CONTINUOUS type meters. It is updated by the BDI whenever the asset is validated and as such should provide a near real time reflection of the current life information for the asset. The PLUSAASSETTIMESINCE records are only updated by the BDI if the option: TSX is included with the list of "ACM Options" in the BDI Instance configuration. The table contains the following attributes: Parameter Description ASSETID The Asset identifier (ASSET.ASSETID). ASSETNUM The Asset number (ASSET.ASSETNUM). SITEID The Site in which the asset resides (ASSET.SITEID). METERNAME The continuous meter name. LIFETODATE The current meter total for asset. SINCEINSTALL The number of meter units accumlated since the last asset installation date. SINCELASTREPAIR The number of meter units accumlated since the asset was last repaired. SINCELASTOVERHAUL The number of meter units accumlated since the asset was last overhauled. SINCELASTINSPECT The number of meter units accumlated since the asset was last inspected.

A model defines the engineering reference data and the allowable configuration for a type of complex asset. The allowable configuration is sometimes referred to as the "as designed" or "could build" configuration. At the simplest level, a Model consists of: A collection of Build Items representing the tracked (often serialized) components which make up a complex asset. For each Build Item one or more Configuration-managed (CM) Items. A CM Item is typically used to represent a Part Number and can be related to a Rotating Item Master record. For each Build Item one or more Labels which may be used to represent the functional system that the Build Item is part of. One or more Configurations that may represent different Variants of the asset type. A Build Hierarchy formed from the list of Build Items to represent the physical structure of the Asset. Configuration rules defining specific criteria that must be obeyed for the associated Asset to be in a valid configuration. The Model is used as template from which configuration managed assets can be created. The Build Data Interpreter (BDI) validates changes to a configuration-managed asset against the Model definition. This is to ensure that operational changes to the associated assets comply with the allowable configuration, defined in the Model, and any problems are communicated to the user. A model can represent a top-level asset, such as an airplane or a train or it can represent a complex equipment subassembly, such as an engine or a locomotive. Any asset which corresponds to the top level position in a model is often referred to as an "End Item". A default configuration-managed (CM) item is created automatically when a new Model is created. You create and modify CM items in the CM Item Master application. New CM asset hierarchies can be created from a Model using the New Asset Assemblies (CM) application.

Technical records are used to represent and model engineering design changes that effect one or more configuration-managed Assets within Maximo. These changes are often safety critical, time-dependent and may apply to an entire fleet. The tracking of the implementation of these, often safety critical and time-dependent, engineering changes is extremely important. They can be used to manage a campaign of changes, across the assets affected, so that the work can be performed, tracked and managed efficiently. A Technical Record consists of: Header Information Information including the purpose of the Technical Record, its type and whether it's compliance it mandatory or optional. Applicability A series of information describing which positions, parts (CM Items), Models and variants the Technical Record applies to. This is used to identify which assets within the system will be impacted once the Technical Record is made active. Maintenance Plan A definition of what is required to carry out the required work and when it should be completed by. This is used to create a PM record, for the affected asset, so the work can be planned and scheduled accordingly. Asset Status A record of the status of the required work against individual assets within the system. A list of the status of all Technical Records against an individual asset is displayed in the Assets (CM) on the Modification Status tab.

Installs and Removals of configuration-managed assets are performed using a dedicated Object Structure: PLUSAMXAPISAONOFF and associated processing class. The example below gives examples of removals and installs from the Rapid Transit Metro Train (RTMT) asset created using the example in the New Asset Assemblies load topic: Rapid Transit Metro Train - Install and Removal Transactions example​ Download Install/Remove Example - MXLoader Install and Removal Transactions data elements​ An explanation of the data elements required to perform removals and installs is described below: Field Description Used for Install or Remove PARENTASSETNUM The parent asset number of the position. Required for both installation and removal transactions. BOTH LCN The LCN value of the position that the asset to be removed is currently installed into. The LCN value is optional if a LABEL and POSITION value is specfied. Note that if LCN is omitted it is recommended that the combination of the LABEL and POSITION uniquely identifies the position the removal/install will be performed against. BOTH LABEL The label of the position. Ignored if LCN is specfied. BOTH POSITION The position value of the build position that the asset is to be removed from. BOTH ASSETNUM The asset number of the asset that is to be removed. If this is not specified whichever asset currently resides in the position identified will be removed. REMOVE REMOVEASSET Must be set to 1 if a removal is being performed (false for installs). REMOVE OFFTIME The transaction date and time that the asset removal took place. REMOVE REMWONUM A work order number to which the removal transaction is to be associated with. REMOVE INSTALLASSET The asset to be installed if an installation is required. INSTALL ONTIME The transaction date and time that the asset installation took place. INSTALL INSTWONUM A work order number to which the install transaction is to be associated with. INSTALL

This page gives instructions, and an example, on how Models and related data can be loaded through the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF). A Model represents the as-designed configuration of a complex asset. An individual Model consists of a series of data elements, some of which must be loaded in a specific order. In order to facilitate the loading of a Model, an MXLoader Excel template is provided in the link below. The example provided gives the as-designed configuration representing a Rapid Transit Metro Train (RTMT): Rapid Transit Metro Train - Model Example​ Download RTMT Model - MXLoader An explanation of the individual data elements and worksheets contained within the MXLoader file is described below. The worksheets are ordered in the necessary way to support the loading of the Models individual data elements. Items​ The Items worksheet provides the mechanism to load Item Master records. These must be loaded first as the CM Items which are loaded in the second worksheet reference these Rotating Item Master records. If the default Item Status (defined in the Organization record within Maximo) is PENDING (and not) ACTIVE then it is recommended that the status of the Rotating Items is changed from PENDING to ACTIVE within the Item Master application. This is so the option "Roll New Status to Organizations and Inventory?" can be chosen to ensure the status of the Item is set to ACTIVE for all records related to the Item. CM Items​ The CM Items worksheet is used to create or update CM Item Master records. These must be loaded prior to loading the Model iteself. Model​ The Model worksheet is used to create the main Model record: PLUSACMMODEL The primary key attributes of a Model are: MODEL, ITEMSETID Build Items​ A Build Item represents a component or assembly. It is used as part of the definition ofthe hierarchical structure of a Model. Each Build Item must reference at least one Label or CM Item. Labels​ Each Build Item must be related to at least one Label. A label is used (together with the Build Item name and Postiion) to identify a specific component within the build hierarchy of a model. It may represent the functional system or some other manufacturer provided coding system. If there is more than one Label for a Build Item then the combination of Label and Default for Position should be unique. CM Items - Build Items​ The "CM Items - Build Items" worksheet is used to load the CM Items related to each Build Item. There must be at least one CM Item for each Build Item. If more than one CM Item is specified for a Build Item then it is recommended that one is marked as the default. Each CM Item, related to a specifc Build Item, performs the same fit, form and function and are by default two-way interchangeable. Build Hierarchy​ The Build Hierarchy is used to define the hierarchy of positions which make up the as-designed configuration represented by the Model. It is typically structured in such a way as to represent the physical structure of the asset. Each line in the worksheet represents an indiviudal "Build Position". The LCN is used to determine the parent/child relationship between build positions and as such should be unique. It is recommended that if the same Build Item is used mulitple times within the same parent assembly, at the same level of indenture, then a unique Position value is used for each build position. This is so users can easily identify which position is being referenced without ambiguity. Variants​ The Variants worksheet is used to load one or more VARIANT Configuration for each Model. Each Model must have at least one Variant Configuration which is non-abstract to allow users to create Assets using the Model. Revisions​ At least one ACTIVE revision record must exist for each Model before users are able to create Assets from it. Configuration Rules​ Configuration Rules define additional criteria that must be obeyed for the Asset to be deemed to be in valid configuration. The configuration rules within a Model are defined within the context of a specific revision of the Model. Each rule is applicable to the revision which it was defined against, and in addition, all later revisions of the Model. This is unless a later rule of the same type exists to override this. A full matrix of the configuration rules, which it is possible to define, is provided in the separate BDI topic "Configuration Rule Matrix". Explanation of PLUSAMXACMAPPLE data attributes. Attribute Description CONFIGRULE A string representation of the configuration rule. The string contains the rule type, and the various data elements which are needed to make up the rule. The rule is interprested by the inbound Object Structure processing class to determine the data required. APPLETYPE A two character code which identifies the rule (applicability element) type. RULEPOSITIVE Indicates if the rule is negative or positive. Rules are normally negative to indicate an exception to the standard behaviour. REVISION The Revision of the Model to which the rule relates. Rules are applied to the revision indicated and any subsequent revisions unless a rule of the same type supercedes this. ISPRIMARY Indicates if the rule is a Primary or Secondary Rule. Most rules are defined to be primary. Specific rule types have the option to define a secondary rule which extends the primary rule to provide further restrictions. Model Flags​ Model Flags are used to indicate specific Yes or No type options which exist against a specific position in relation to a Model and a Configuration. The most common usage is to indicate whether a build position is mandatory for specific Variant (or Role). Attribute Description VARIATION The name of the configuration (normally a Variant name). LCN The LCN of the Build Position within the Model to which the flag record relates FOREIGNENTITY This should always be set to: PLUSACMCONFIG REVISION The Revision of the Model to which the flag rule relates. Rules are applied to the revision indicated and any subsequent revisions unless a flag rule of the same type for the same build position and variant supercedes this. FLAGTYPE The type of Flag, options are: MANDATORY - If the position is mandatory CREATEWO - When a mandatory position becomes empty, indicates whether a WO should be created automatically (against the parent assembly). EVENTSINACTIVE - If true all PMs for the Asset in the position will be made INACTIVE. ALLOWANYPART - If true the system should consider any CM Item installed into the position to be valid. FLAG 1 or 0 to indicate the flag value Full Model​ The Full Model tab demonstrates how the main data elements of a Model can be loaded in one worksheet/transaction. Note that CM Items (and related Item Master) records referenced by the Model must still be loaded prior to the Model. Applicability Rule (PLUSACMAPPLE) and Flag Rules (PLUSACMFLAG) must also be loaded after the full model.

The New Asset Assemblies (NAA) application enables a user to create a CM managed asset hierarchy from a Model. This page gives instructions, and an example, on how New Asset Assemblies records can be loaded through the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF). This includes the top level asset record and related meters and also the sub assembly (child) assets and their related meters. In order to facilitate the loading of a New Asset Assemblies record, an MXLoader Excel template is provided in the link below. The example provided enables the creation of a Rapid Transit Metro Train (RTMT) type Asset and it's sub assembly asset hierarchy: Rapid Transit Metro Train - New Asset Assemblies Example​ Download RTMT New Asset Assemblies - MXLoader An explanation of the individual data elements and worksheets contained within the MXLoader file is described below. The worksheets are ordered in the necessary way to support the loading of the New Asset Assemblies data. New Asset​ The New Asset worksheet is used to create the main New Asset Assemblies record (PLUSANEWASSET). Data on this record will ultimately be used to create an ASSET record in Maximo. The record contains the asset number, serial number, registration (if specified as required in the associated Model) and other CM Related data eg, CM Item, Model, Variant etc. New Asset Meters​ The New Asset Meters worksheet is used to specifiy the data that will be used to create the Asset Meter records for the top level asset. These are limited to CONTINUOUS type Meters. Meters can also be automatically added to the Asset by way of a Meter Group which is linked to the Item Master record associated with the CM Item. ubassemblies​ The Subassemblies worksheet contains the information required to create the asset assembly hiearchy below the top level asset. Each sub assembly asset needs to specify it's parent asset, CM Item and serial number. To indentify the position in the Model to which the asset corresponds the Label and Position can be specified if the combination of these values uniquely identifies the position within the model. If it does not it is preferable to specify the build identifier (PLUSANEWSUB.BUILDID). This is the identifier of the position within the Model (PLUSACMBUILD.PLUSACMBUILDID). Note that the sub assemblies can be generated through the UI and then queried using MXLoader. The sheet can then be updated to specify the serial number, CM Item, Install Date etc of each subassembly asset before it is then sent back in Maximo. Subassembly Meters​ The Subassembly Meters worksheet specifies the Continuous meters records to create against each sub assembly. There is one line per asset per meter. The Anchor Count should reflect the life of the asset at the Anchor Date. The Since New value should be set to the life of the asset at the time of asset creation. This will be used to create a METERREADING record of type ACTUAL with the Since New Value and a Reading Date = to the system date/time at asset creation.

ACM provides dedicated Object Structures which can be used to load relevant data loaded through the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF). They can be used to load data such as CM Items, Models, New Asset Assemblies, Master PMs etc. Specific explanations and examples are provided using MXLoader.

Object Structure Description PLUSAMXCMITEM CM Item Master PLUSAMXMODEL Models PLUSAMXPLUSACMFLAG Model Flag Rules (Eg Mandatory positions for configuration). PLUSAMXACMAPPLE Model Configuration Rules (Applicability Elements) PLUSAMXNEWASSET New Asset Assemblies PLUSAMXASSET Assets PLUSAMXSAONOFF Install / Remove transactions for CM Managed Assets PLUSAMXMASTERPM Master PMs PLUSAMPM PMs PLUSAMXPMNEXT Used to initialize/set when the PM for a configuration-managed assets was last done and/or is next due. PLUSAMXTR Technical Records PLUSAMXTRASSET Tecnical Record Asset Status. Used to record embodiment status for Technical Records against Assets

documents.t: This page gives instructions, and an example of how to initialize PMs for configuration-managed Assets using the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF). The example below gives examples of how to intialize preventive maintenance (PM) records for configuration-managed assets. Initialising a PM involves setting when it was last completed (if applicable) and when it is next due. Peforming this action through the MIF enables a bulk initialisation of PMs, for example when a new asset is brought into service and many PMs are created automatically. The example includes data to intialise the calendar based 12 month inspection and also the meter based overhaul PMs for the bogies within the train.

Download Initialising PMs Example - MXLoader An explanation of the individual data elements and worksheets contained within the MXLoader file is described below. Field Description MASTERPM and PMNUM The parent asset number of the position. Required for both installation and removal transactions. In the case a Master PM is specifed the system will use the combination of Asset number, Master PM number, and Site ID to uniquely identify a PM record. ASSETNUM The asset number of the configuration-managed asset. LASTCOMPDATE The date at which the PM last completed. This is optional. PLUSANEWNEXTDUEDATE The date and time at which the PM is next Due. This is an optional value for calendar based PM frequencies. If the Next Due Date is not specified then the system will calculated this by adding the PM time based frequency to the Last Completion Date to determine the Next Due Date. PMMETER.METERNAME The Meter Name for a PM with a meter based frequency. PMMETER.PLUSANEWLASTDONECOUNT The meter total for the asset at the point the PM was last completed. PMMETER.PLUSANEWNEXTDUECOUNT The meter total at which the PM is next due for the asset. If this is not specified the system will use the meter total at last completion + PM Meter frequency to determine the next due count.

documents.t: This page gives instructions, and an example of how to create Master PMs for configuration-managed Assets using the Maximo Integration Framework (MIF). Master PMs for configuration-managed assets are associated with one or more CM Items. This enables the system to automatically create the PMs for each Asset using the relationship with the CM Item. The example below gives examples of Master PMs for the Rapid Transit Metro Train (RTMT). Two examples are given: A yearly (12 month) inspection for the the end item (train) asset. The alert and warning intervals are set to: Alert 10 days before Due Date (a work order is automatically generated by the BDI at the alert interval). Warning Interval 5 days before due date. A bogie overhaul, which is required every 500,000 KM. This task is related to two CM Items for the Motor and Trailer Bogies. The alert and warning interval are set to 5000KM and 2500KM before due count respectively.

Download Master PM Example - MXLoader Once the Master PMs are created (and made active) and the BDI validates the asset the system will automatically create the necessary PMs for each asset using the link to the CM Item. When PMs are created automatically they are marked as needing reviewed (ENR - Event Needs Review problem code is returned by the BDI). The next topic describes how the PMs can be initialized using the MIF to set when they were last performed and next due.

The diagram below give a pictoral representation of the main design concepts of Asset Configuration Manager. The top blue section represents the engineering reference data and data elements used to define the as-designed or allowable configuration of a complex asset. The bottom red section represents the operational data which which is used to track and manage the as-built and as-maintained assets. Between these two sets of data is the Build Data Intepreter (BDI). The function of the BDI is to compare the two sets of data to determine and report a configuration status and any problems with the configuration managed asset(s).

ACM is designed to minimise the data required to define the as-designed configuration. This is accomplished by the use of Models, Variants and sub models. Maximo Asset Configuration Manager (ACM) is an add-on solution for the Maximo Manage application of the IBM Maximo Application Suite. It is designed to manage the complex configuration and lifecycle of highly regulated, safety-critical, and configuration-dependent assets—such as those found in aviation, transportation, and defense industries.

ACM extends Maximo’s core asset management capabilities by introducing configuration-aware asset tracking and control. Its main features include: Configuration Management: Track and manage the hierarchical structure and configuration of complex assets, including serialized components and assemblies. Life-Limited Parts Tracking: Monitor usage and life limits of critical components to ensure compliance with safety and maintenance regulations. Effectivity Management: Apply changes to assets based on specific conditions such as time, usage, or serial number ranges. Change Control: Manage engineering changes and ensure traceability of modifications across the asset lifecycle. Maintenance Planning Integration: Align configuration data with maintenance schedules to ensure accurate and timely servicing. Compliance and Audit Readiness: Maintain a complete history of asset configurations and changes for regulatory compliance and audit purposes.

Implementing ACM provides organizations with: Improved Asset Visibility: Gain a detailed, real-time view of asset configurations and their operational status. Regulatory Compliance: Ensure adherence to industry standards and regulations through robust tracking and documentation. Reduced Operational Risk: Minimize the risk of failure or non-compliance by proactively managing life-limited parts and configuration changes. Optimized Maintenance: Enhance maintenance planning and execution by aligning it with actual asset configurations. Enhanced Decision-Making: Leverage accurate configuration data to support strategic asset management decisions.

ACM is ideal for industries where asset configuration is critical to safety, performance, and compliance, including: Aerospace and Defense Rail and Transit Marine Space and Satellite Technologies Oil and Gas
